summary: Seema Alavi is a historian who earned her doctorate at the University of Cambridge (~1987–1991). She taught at the University of Delhi and Jawaharlal Nehru University, and was a history professor at Jamia Millia Islamia (~2005–2012) and Ashoka University (~2020).

Seigai Omura worked in art history, Buddhist studies, and Sinology, studying at Tokyo University of the Arts (~1889–1893) under Umpei Shinma and Kanō Tomonobu. He taught there as assistant professor (1896) and professor (1905), and founded the Bussho Kankōkai.

Seiichi Mizuno specialized in archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, earning degrees from Kyoto University (~1925–1928, Litt.D. 1962) under Kosaku Hamada. He worked at Kyoto University's Institute for Research in Humanities (1938, 1961) and served as university professor (1949–1968).

Seiichi Yagi is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1955). He held posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1966–1993), Kanto Gakuin University, and Toin University of Yokohama.

Seiichiro Ono studied at the University of Tokyo (~1914–1917, LL.D. 1933) under Eiichi Makino, Daito Shimaji, Kanae Tada, and Jōkan Chikazumi. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1922–1951) and Aichi Gakuin University (1957–1977).

Seiji Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Komazawa University (attested 1986). He held posts at Komazawa University (attested 1990) and served as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995).
Seiji Kumagai specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Kyoto University (~2003–2008), where he later served as an associate professor (~2013).
Seiji Nemoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, and Japanology. He studied at Meiji University (~1968–1972) and later served as a professor at the University of Tsukuba (~1999–2015).
Seiji Tanaka studied under Bruno Petzold. He later held academic posts at Aoyama Gakuin University (~1960–1968) and Asia University (~1968).
Seijun Ishii is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (~1977–1987). He later served as a professor at Komazawa University (~2004).
Seikaku Hirata was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1947–1950) under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu and Bokuo Seki. He later held a post at Hanazono University (~1970–2000).

Sein Tin was a linguist who studied at the University of Rangoon (~1920–1923), under Pe Maung Tin (1924–1927), and at Christ Church, Oxford (~1927–1929), having earlier attended Basic Education High School No. 9 Mawlamyine.

Seiran Ouchi worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He served as jikō at Nishi Hongan-ji, founded Hoshi Sodan (1874) and Meikyo Shinshi (1875), and served as president of Toyo University (1914–1918).

Seiren Matsunami was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (-1930) under Naoshiro Tsuji and Walther Schubring. He held posts as professor at Kyushu University (attested 1965) and Rissho University (attested 1972).

Seishi Karashima studied Buddhist philology at the University of Tokyo, Cambridge, and Peking University under mentors including K. R. Norman and Oskar von Hinüber. He was long-term director and professor at Soka University's International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology (~1994–2019).

Seishin Kato, a Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Toyo University (~1888–1891) and Shingiyaha Daigakurin (~1891–1893). He served as president of Buzan University (1918, 1923), Taisho University (1940), and Toyo University (1952, 1955).
Seitatsu Matsunami is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He served as an assistant at the University of Tokyo and as a professor at Taisho University (attested 1992).

Seizan Yanagida specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, studying at Hanazono, Otani, and Kyoto University under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu. He was professor at Hanazono University, Kyoto University (1976–1986), and director of the International Research Institute for Zen Buddhism (~1988–1996).

Sempa Dorje is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Ram Shankar Tripathi. He served as a professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1977, 1990–1998).
Sen Wang was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Peking University (~1931–1935) and later served as a professor at Minzu University of China (~1952–1978).
